items.reason: Artifacts assigns type "exploration" and orders it between spec and progress.
The dashboard consumes the same ordered artifact list.
The orphan-markdown validator explicitly exempts exploration.md.
Other validation rules and rejection of unlisted markdown remain intact.
ExploreRequested reads the set-level explore boolean.
Automatic exploration requires an explicit true value.
ExplorerOverride uses the shared agents-and-effort directive shape.
The guide documents both keys and explicitly distinguishes opt-in from opt-out.
The guide states the shared-seam and later-task dependency rule.
Shared constants supply names, and a guide-to-manifest test checks agreement.
The command starts a fresh agent with the task listing, task bodies, and available spec.
The explorer template requests all five specified observations.
The template requires path-or-symbol claims, approximately one page, and observed-tree identification.
The explorer template requests no prior-art investigation or section.
Successful exploration atomically replaces the flat exploration.md file.
Explore has its own captured-run phase, spend bucket, and retry-cap records.
Standalone exploration bypasses both participation gates.
Failed, timed-out, and interrupted runs return without replacing the report.
The command test joins agent execution, report replacement, and captured-run metadata.
Implement prompts conditionally include the existing report’s path and explanation.
Prompt construction checks report existence without reading its content.
The prompt limits corrections to lines this attempt made false.
The edit boundary explicitly allows the report alongside the task file.
The existing prior-art block remains byte-for-byte unchanged.
Assist includes the exploration pointer beside refinement and recent progress.
Implement and assist goldens cover report-present and report-absent cases.
Exploration runs only before the loop; clearing an initial HITL or failed-task gate can then start implementation without exploration.
An existing report bypasses the explore runner and its spending.
Undeclared sets bypass automatic exploration.
The dedicated work.explore group defaults enabled when the group or enabled key is absent.
The machine switch disables automatic passes without disabling standalone exploration.
Agent and effort resolution follows CLI, manifest, then configuration precedence.
The automatic phase explicitly skips human-completed sets.
Report existence controls reuse without comparing recorded and current trees.
Whole-drain tests assert one pass without a report and zero passes with one.
The shared fallback runner applies the standard retry cap and delays.
Exhausted exploration without a report derives EXPLORE-FAILED and stops the drain.
Parking derives from captured-run metadata and report absence without schema changes.
EXPLORE-FAILED is distinct from the unchanged BLOCKED status.
Daemon and automatic READY selection exclude EXPLORE-FAILED rows.
attendableHITLTaskSets ignores row status and can select a parked set with an eligible HITL task.
The failed pass appends one phase-and-reason progress record; subsequent drains do not repeat it.
The forwarded skip-explore flag bypasses exploration and an existing park.
Writing a report or retracting the declaration removes the derived park.
CONTEXT.md includes EXPLORE-FAILED in both stop and automatic-skip lists.
The mark and its reason occupy separate fields and render together.
Sets without an exploration declaration resolve to an empty mark.
Refresh resolves the mark once and propagates it to the four requested surfaces.
Parked rows retain their mark in shared Work status rendering and detail rendering.
ExplorationSection suppresses the report pointer and recorded tree for hand-explored sets without an explore declaration.
gateExplorePreamble similarly hides an existing report when the set has no exploration declaration.
Successful runs carry the reported verdict, so later report deletion triggers exploration instead of parking.

scores.rationale: Broad tests and good reuse of existing mechanisms, but gate-resumption, fallback-selection, and report-visibility gaps remain.
